claim: The Stage B catalog plan is superseded by `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-02-cas-stage-b-remaining.md`, which is the execution authority for remaining Stage-B work.

The catalog entry's incarnation is the opaque physical `life_id` shared by the ref layer and namespace files; the logical `RootNamespace` remains in catalog entries and in-memory `NamespaceLifeId` values but is absent from life-owned object keys.

The final namespace-owned layout uses immutable stream objects under `cas/ns/stream/<life_id>/{_log,_snap,_cleanup}` and point/path-addressed state under `cas/ns/state/<life_id>/{_ckpt,_files}`; `_cleanup` is transitional and is removed by the removal lifecycle.
Manifest objects retain `(namespace, mount-epoch, build-sequence)` identity and globally unique build identities, while loose mountpoint objects remain outside namespace ownership and unqualified.

The layout transition to opaque `life_id` keys is a recreate-only generation-6 cut, and the removal lifecycle's `_cleanup` deletion and `ref_lives` fold-seal transition is a separate recreate-only generation-7 wire cut; older generations are refused rather than dual-read or migrated.

The `_ckpt` object is a fixed-size product of scalar monotone facts whose encoded size is `O(1)` in the number of refs, files, transactions, and writer epochs; maps and other cardinality-growing state belong in separate immutable objects or ledgers.

Namespace-file incarnation qualification must preserve the existing direct-object operation profile: no catalog request per file operation, no ref-log append, no blob upload, no folder-manifest rewrite, and unchanged backend request counts.

This series does not move namespace files into the ref log, add folder-state manifests or a `_raw_files` object family, change `MergeTreeDeduplicationLog`, merge `Poisoned` into wedge, refactor `RefApplyState`, or remove the plain-object component.
`Poisoned` is distinct from wedge: it means a durable transaction may be missing from the cached view, so it blocks snapshot publication and triggers re-recovery.

The destructive GC round remains sequential in this series: it adds no `MultiDelete`, batch-delete API, parallel delete fan-out, or delete-side concurrency, so the soak establishes a per-operation baseline for a later optimization round.

The catalog has states `Creating`, `Live`, and `Removing`; each `CatalogEntry` contains a logical namespace, a random nonzero 128-bit incarnation, and a creator fence identity exactly when its state is `Creating`.
`RefCatalog` is the token-CAS object at key `cas/ref_catalog`, with entries in canonical order by namespace bytes and no duplicate namespaces.

Catalog admission independently requires `encoded_catalog_bytes <= catalog_object_cap` and `fold_fixed_bytes + Σ worst_case_entry_reservation <= fold_seal_object_cap`; equality is accepted, capacity overflow is loud, and removal is never refused.

Namespace creation consists of a token-CAS insertion of a `Creating` entry with a fresh incarnation and creator fence, creation of `<ns>/<inc>/_ckpt`, and a token-CAS transition from `Creating` to `Live` that rechecks the creator's admission generation and the observed catalog token.
A namespace in `Creating` must not publish ref data; stale-`Creating` reconciliation is permitted only after the creator fence is terminal and must use an exact observed-entry token.

If namespace birth publishes `_ckpt` and then its ref-log `PUT` fails, the failed birth can leave durable `_ckpt` debris; the creation lifecycle must delete that `_ckpt` for a never-born namespace without deleting a live namespace's checkpoint.

The final physical key grammar is `cas/ns/stream/<life_id>/_log/<txn>.zst`, `cas/ns/stream/<life_id>/_snap/<txn>.zst`, `cas/ns/state/<life_id>/_ckpt.zst`, and `cas/ns/state/<life_id>/_files/<relative-name>`; the transitional `cas/ns/stream/<life_id>/_cleanup/<txn>` family is removed by Task 5.

`_snap` remains under `stream/` because it is immutable and sequence-addressed, is grouped with logs for recovery hints and covered-object cleanup, and avoids a second hot LIST; the stream/state split is by access pattern, not ownership.

A reverse catalog index maps every catalog state to `life_id -> NamespaceLifeId{name, incarnation}`; a duplicate current `life_id` is `CORRUPTED_DATA`, makes both rows unresolvable, and causes catalog mutations, REBUILD, decommission, fold adoption, and destructive GC to fail closed.

The hot GC round completes one `LIST(cas/ns/stream/)`, then takes one authoritative full-catalog `{token, value}` cut; `Live` and `Removing` entries in that cut are admitted, while listed ids absent from the later cut are inert dead-life debris and are not admitted or a reason to defer.

The removal lifecycle is `Creating → Live → Removing → absent`, and a pure walk-plan constructor creates exactly one `ref_lives` row for every catalog entry in `Live` or `Removing`, with no row for `Creating` or an absent id.

Every GC invocation acquires and validates the lease and adopted seal, conclusively drains eligible `Removing` rows, completes `LIST(cas/ns/stream/)`, takes one fresh full-catalog cut, builds the ref walk plan, and only then decides `DEFER` or performs fold, seal, and adoption.

A complete `Removing` row may be exact-CAS-deleted only when the matching adopted parent life row contains cleanup evidence and no durable hold; ambiguous or conflicting catalog CAS outcomes are resolved conclusively before successor publication.

Removal completion performs no namespace-owned physical LIST, physical delete, physical-empty proof, or second deletion window; `_ckpt`, stream, and namespace-file residue is leak-only janitor work, while orphan manifests remain the orphan sweep's work.
A namespace rebirth receives a new opaque `life_id`, so an adopted predecessor row cannot be inherited by the successor and stale predecessor handles cannot target successor state.

The perpetual janitor scans `LIST(cas/ns/)` in bounded pages, stores one cleanup-only opaque pagination token in `GcMaintenanceState`, and takes a fresh catalog read after each page before classifying and exact-token-deleting candidates.
A valid janitor page under destructive suppression does not advance its cursor, preventing alternating `DEFER` and fold rounds from permanently skipping a dead page.

Recovery grounding uses `_ckpt.checkpoint_snapshot_id` as the only snapshot base and `_ckpt.committed_through` as the inclusive frontier; it never derives a base, genesis, frontier, or stop condition from stream `LIST` results.
`Creating` namespaces are never recovered or published; `Live` and `Removing` namespaces require a readable `_ckpt` with `life_epoch`, and a life id absent from the catalog is not recovered.

A committed ref chunk follows log `PUT` → `_ckpt.committed_through` GET/CAS → in-memory install and acknowledgement → allocation of the next id; an unresolved log/frontier window remains in `NeedsRecovery`.

The snapshot publication unit preserves the order immutable snapshot body durable → `_ckpt` advances via `publishCkptContribution` → new snapshot adopted in memory, and the two durable effects are not separately callable.
A reader holds a `NamespaceLifeId` handle and may return stale data or `NotFound` after removal, but must never read a newer incarnation and must not perform a hot-path fence or catalog read.

Destructive cleanup of a current catalog life revalidates the life and fence immediately before every per-key `deleteExact`; the dead-life janitor may use a page-level catalog cut because catalog-before-object publication and non-reused `life_id` provide the stronger ordering proof.
Delayed namespace-file writes capture the exact `NamespaceLifeId` at admission; a callback must not capture only `RootNamespace` and resolve the life when `finalizeImpl` runs.

Probe A is deleted because catalog-authoritative discovery and LIST-independent recovery make its second full stream LIST irrelevant to correctness; B1/B2 accounting and the mount-time capability probe remain.

The destructive gate remains `suppress_destructive = anomalies || carried_holds || !frontier_complete`; the Stage B change permits `frontier_complete` to become true from catalog proof but does not weaken any suppression term.

Before the authoritative flip, an empty catalog can make `result.frontier_complete = universe_authoritative && result.frontier_proven == result.frontier_namespaces` evaluate as `0 == 0`, falsely clearing destructive suppression; an empty universe must not count as a complete frontier.

Decommission enumerates a claimed server root's catalog entries exactly, resumes unfinished `Removing` writer work under the claimed fence when `_ckpt` exists, leaves completed removal to GC, and performs a final exact catalog token check before slot retirement.

R3 orphan-manifest cleanup exact-GETs and decodes the manifest first, feeds its `BlobRef`s through a neutral nomination input, adopts nominations in the round's `gc/state` CAS, and only then performs exact-token deletion.

The Stage B destructive-baseline report must measure sequential GC costs by phase and S3 verb, name untimed spans rather than estimate them, and rank falsifiable opportunities for a later `MultiDelete` or delete-concurrency round.
The TLA+ phase is a pre-C++ gate: every new invariant must be observed red under a dedicated `_sab_*` configuration before its green configuration is trusted.
The writer/recovery model replaces `nextId` with a single at-most-one in-flight `pendingSlot`, derives `NextSlot` from durable and sealed ids, and tracks ambiguous attempts in `ambiguousEver`.

A recovery walk uses `ckpt` as its base, advances by arithmetic expected-id reads rather than listing hints, and closes the epoch by occupying the next slot with a seal or adopting a matching in-flight straggler.
The model's cleanup guard permits only log ids at or below `ckpt.base`, and a missing base with an unchanged checkpoint token is corruption rather than a normal recovery outcome.
In the fold model, a page scan is only a hint that may omit keys; arithmetic `WalkStep` advances the cursor by expected transaction id and supplies the authoritative delta candidates.

The fold's blob in-degree is pool-wide and is computed from fixed `EdgeOf` roles over folded keys; condemnation requires every table frontier proof and no hold, while deletion also requires no hold and two-phase pacing.
A fold hold set after an expected-next 404 with a higher durable id may be cleared only by folding through the offending id; clearing it on another absent probe is unsafe.

The catalog model mints a fresh incarnation on each create, creates `_ckpt` before going live, allows stale-creator reconciliation only after the creator fence dies, and lets the janitor delete only objects whose incarnation is not current.
The stale-leader cleanup model makes recreation safe structurally: stale deletes capture and target the old incarnation, while reuse of an incarnation is the sabotage that violates rebirth safety.
Recovery installation and wedge retries are guarded by the fence generation captured at recovery start; a successor seal conclusively rejects an old-generation retry.

The TLA phase summary is a pass only when every green configuration is green and every `_sab_*` configuration reports its expected violation; listing-trust audits record the exact action and premise for every model.

Namespace-file rebirth safety is closed by keys of the form `cas/ns/state/<life_id>/_files/<relative-name>` and by binding reads and delayed writes to the exact `NamespaceLifeId` selected before rebirth.
Writer cleanup requires an in-memory duty queue while the mount lives and a successor-seal path for crash remnants; a build must not be retired while its owner-grant outcome is uncertain.
The existing `~PartWriteTxn` unconditionally retires a build while an owner grant may be wedged-Unresolved, and staged-body cleanup can swallow failures until the epoch seals.

The orphan sweep's neutral nomination input is accounting-neutral: it does not consume ref-transaction ordinals or increment unmatched-remove accounting for an already-absent edge, while retaining exact source-edge identities.
A different token at an immutable manifest key is illegal ABA; the sweep retains the manifest and surfaces the condition instead of deleting it.

REBUILD can currently condemn a physically listed blob when a live manifest is hidden from LIST, and the durable remedy is an authoritative build/upload registry; until then REBUILD cannot reclaim manifest-less orphan blobs safely.

A decommissioned server-root slot cannot retire while any catalog entry owned by that root remains; a `Removing` entry without a terminal record is resumable writer work when `_ckpt` exists and is corruption when `_ckpt` is absent.
Wedge retry is demand-driven: a permanently quiet wedged namespace retries on its next caller or an independently occurring remount, because the unresolved operation was never acknowledged.
Before incarnation qualification, `groupRefKeys` grouped listed ref keys by `parsed->id.ns.string()` and discarded `parsed->id.incarnation`, merging old and reborn lives into one `RefTableListing`.

The parser remains catalog-independent and accepts a dead incarnation's syntactically valid key; fold and REBUILD filter keys whose parsed incarnation does not match the current catalog entry before grouping.

`_ckpt.life_epoch` can receive legitimate contributions from both `CasRefCatalog::completeCreation` and the first `NamespaceBirth` chunk, and treating every different present value as corruption would wedge resumed creation and restart-before-first-write sequences.

The register's 2026-07-31 ruling for `_ckpt.life_epoch` was to reject decreases and let a higher monotone value win, because a lower contribution indicates a fenced-out writer whose contribution landed.
`ensureRefTableRecovered` and `resolveNamespaceLife` can mint a `Live` catalog entry and durable `_ckpt` from a read path, so `existsFile` on a never-born namespace can perform durable writes.
Because read-created catalog entries are not reclaimed, reads against nonexistent tables can grow the one pool-wide catalog without bound and exhaust admission capacity for legitimate creations.

The read-side fix for read-created catalog entries is to resolve a namespace without creating one and return an optional life only when the namespace exists and its files are readable; the decision was to be made before the removal lifecycle.

A current catalog life can have an empty key space while a dead incarnation of the same logical namespace has objects; filtering dead keys and walking the current life can then falsely prove the frontier complete and enable destruction.

The mismatch hazard requires a detector that records names seen at dead incarnations and raises an anomaly when the current incarnation contributes neither a listed ref object nor `_ckpt`; the authority-only predicate does not cover this case.

If the catalog is absent, a sentinel fallback such as `stageATransition(ns)` can make real-incarnation namespaces look empty and let a damaged catalog produce a complete frontier; an un-cataloged namespace must be unproven rather than walked at a fabricated key.

An un-cataloged namespace during ordinary removal is a legitimate transient state when removal evidence exists; anomaly reporting must distinguish that state from an un-cataloged namespace with no removal evidence.
The S42 sweep defect strands folded `+1` blob edges when an orphan manifest is swept, so orphan nomination must directly account for those source edges.

The TLA writer/recovery model retired its rev.4 and rev.6 configurations because v9 semantics superseded them, and `LatePredecessorPut` changed from expected-fail to a green case under the new seal and arithmetic-walk rules.
